clue.text: Inclined to blow one's top…

parts.note: reads as a hot-tempered person, but a mountain that blows its top is one that throws out lava

explanation.surface: A description of someone with a short fuse who is liable to lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow one's top' is the idiom for losing your temper, but read literally it is a mountain blasting off its summit. The clue runs on into 5 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain liable to explode from its summit is a fire-mountain type, one given to eruption.

clue.text: Attest to a very absorbing Kipling poem

indicators.note: the first word takes in the poem, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
'If—' is Rudyard Kipling's best-known poem

explanation.surface: Bearing witness to a deeply engrossing poem by Kipling.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm the truth of something is to bear witness to it.

clue.text: Had fun being taken around the old menagerie

indicators.note: the guiding word goes round the ark

parts.note: led means taken or guided
Noah's Ark held animals of every kind, an ancient menagerie

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys themselves on a guided tour of an old zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken around' reads as one phrase, but 'taken' gives the letters and 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To play around or frolic is to have a good time mischievously.

clue.text: The spirit of Islington

parts.note: sounds like the character of a London borough, but names a heavenly being that is also a district of Islington

explanation.surface: A phrase about the character of a north London district.
explanation.walkthrough: The Angel is an area and Tube station in Islington, north London, named after an old coaching inn; it is also a heavenly spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavenly spirit shares its name with a district of Islington in London.

clue.text: Indecorative time of life

parts.note: a plain, unadorned period of life, but read 'Indecorative' as 'in' plus 'decorative', a synonym for fancy, with 'time of life' as definition

explanation.surface: An undecorated period in someone's life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indecorative' looks like a word meaning plain, but split it: IN, then 'decorative', which is FANCY; 'time of life' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Early childhood is the first period in a person's life.

clue.text: … and does so

parts.note: carries on from 1 Across: the hot-tempered mountain actually blows its top

explanation.surface: A continuation saying the short-tempered person does in fact lose their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 1 Across: what the explosive mountain does is blow its top, that is, it bursts out in fire and lava.
explanation.definitionFit: Blowing one's top, for a mountain, means spewing lava; for a person, means bursting into anger.

clue.text: Lifelike it is clear when redeveloped

indicators.note: redeveloping something rebuilds it in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A building scheme that looks true to life once it has been rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When redeveloped' signals the letters of IT IS CLEAR rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: True to nature or representing things as they actually are.

clue.text: Offer to support, also to reform

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: reforming reshapes, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An offer to back a cause and also to change it.
explanation.walkthrough: PROP, then OSAL, the anagram of ALSO signalled by 'to reform'.
explanation.definitionFit: A suggestion put forward for consideration, or an offer of marriage.

clue.text: Despatches from the field of contention?

definitions.text: Despatches from the field of contention?

parts.words: Despatches from the field of contention?
parts.note: sounds like war reports from a battlefield, but means a referee ordering players off the pitch

explanation.surface: Military dispatches sent home from the front line of a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despatches' suggests war reports, but here is a verb: a referee dismissing a player from the playing field.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee dismisses a player from the pitch, removing them from the game.

clue.text: Exceptional contribution made by king at helm of frigate in trouble

indicators.note: being at the helm of a ship means standing at its front, so this piece leads

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

indicators.note: a ship in trouble is in disarray, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A ruler commanding a ship in difficulties makes an outstanding offering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made by' is only a link; 'frigate in trouble' looks like the picture but is the anagram fodder with its signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uncommon that is given, a present of unusual quality, is an exceptional contribution.

clue.text: Idle accountant leaves macaroon

indicators.note: the accountant leaves the biscuit, so those letters go out of the word

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A lazy accountant walks away from an almond biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' removes CA from MACAROON. 'Idle' is a verb here: in Chambers, to maroon can mean to loiter or idle about.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary sense of the verb is to loaf or hang about doing nothing, a dialect use.

clue.text: I object to an intermediate term

parts.note: I as the object of a verb becomes me
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone protesting at an interim period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object' sounds like a protest, but means the object form of I.
explanation.definitionFit: In maths, the middle quantity between extremes, or an average, is an intermediate value.

clue.text: Self-employed swimmer in France

indicators.note: the swimmer goes inside the name of the country

parts.note: taken as written
an eel is a fish, so a swimmer

explanation.surface: Someone working for themselves who is a swimmer based in France.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works independently for several clients rather than on a payroll.

clue.text: They're used by golfers under pressure

definitions.text: They're used by golfers under pressure

parts.words: They're used by golfers under pressure
parts.note: suggests nervous golfers' clubs, but also household appliances that press clothes with heat and pressure

explanation.surface: A remark about the clubs that golfers reach for when the pressure is on.
explanation.walkthrough: Golfers use clubs of this name, and the domestic appliances for smoothing laundry work by applying pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal-headed golf clubs and laundry pressing appliances share one name.

clue.text: Left clinging girl for a Roman historian

parts.note: Ivy is a girl's name and also a clinging climbing plant

explanation.surface: A clingy girl is abandoned in favour of an ancient historian.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus Livius, known in English by this name, wrote a vast history of Rome.

clue.text: Give effect to a tool

definitions.meaning: to carry out or put into practice

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to carry out a plan; as a noun it means a utensil or instrument.

clue.text: Your's a pint? Rather!

definitions.meaning: asking whether the drink is a full pint and not a half-pint
British slang exclamation of strong agreement, like 'very much so!'

explanation.surface: A pub exchange: asked whether they want a pint, the drinker eagerly agrees.
explanation.walkthrough: Beer in a British pub comes in pints or halves; the slang phrase of emphatic agreement also literally means 'not a half-pint'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally denies a half measure and colloquially means 'certainly' or 'very much'.

clue.text: Antagonise by using wrong reagents

indicators.note: using the reagents in the wrong way, their letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A chemist annoys colleagues by using the wrong chemicals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' signals REAGENTS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone, to make them hostile or unfriendly.

clue.text: It can be picked up on a p ring

definitions.text: It can be picked up on a p ring

parts.words: It can be picked up on a p ring
parts.note: sounds like an item lifted from a ring, but describes the handset lifted when the telephone rings; the stray 'p' is print debris

explanation.surface: Something that can be lifted from a ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A ring' is a phone call: when the telephone rings you pick up the handset.
explanation.definitionFit: The handset of a telephone is lifted when a call comes in.

clue.text: Church eminence…

parts.note: sounds like a senior cleric, but eminence also means a tall structure, here the spire of a church

explanation.surface: A title for a senior churchman, a cardinal perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eminence' is the title of a cardinal, but here means a lofty part of a church building. The clue continues into 21 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tower with a spire rising from a church is its loftiest point.

clue.text: Flowing sort of robe in Spain

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: a river is something flowing

indicators.note: a sort of robe is a variant of it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A loose, flowing type of gown worn in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' signals ROBE rearranged; 'Flowing ... in Spain' points at a Spanish river, with 'in Spain' completing the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ebro is a long river flowing through northern Spain to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: … with one who'll make it to the top

definitions.text: with one who'll make it to the top

parts.words: with one who'll make it to the top
parts.note: joined to 19 Across, the word makes the name of a worker who climbs church towers

explanation.surface: A continuation about an ambitious person bound for success.
explanation.walkthrough: Joined to the church tower of 19 Across this gives the name for a man who climbs tall structures to repair them: he literally reaches the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Added to the church tower word, this gives the trade of a climber who repairs high towers.

clue.text: Water below 52' FRight

clue.text: Heavy woollen cloth for coating an architectural decoration

definitions.meaning: a coarse napped wool fabric used for overcoats
a sculpted or painted band along the top of a wall

explanation.definitionFit: One word names both a thick wool coat fabric and a decorative horizontal band on a building.

clue.text: Implore one "Off with you!"

parts.note: to implore is to beg
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone pleads with a person and then orders them away.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned command to go away.

clue.text: Concerning a ladybird, Mrs Ruff

parts.note: re means about or concerning
read as lady + bird: Eve, the first lady

explanation.surface: A note about a ladybird addressed to a woman named Mrs Ruff.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruff is a wading bird; its female has its own name, so 'Mrs Ruff' is the hen bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The female of the ruff, a sandpiper, has a separate name, as a hen is to a cock.

clue.text: Musical flower girl

parts.note: a rose is a flower
Marie is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl named after a flower who is gifted at music.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose-Marie is a 1924 operetta-style stage show by Friml and Stothart.

clue.text: Maxim of abstainer in low surroundings

indicators.note: the cow's sound forms the surroundings, enclosing the abstainer

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
TT means teetotal, someone abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A teetotaller's saying, delivered in shabby surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' means the cow's call here, not 'base' or 'depressed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A short saying expressing a principle or rule of conduct.

clue.text: Save in a way with floating assets

indicators.note: done in a way, the letters are rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Advice to put money aside in a fashion involving liquid funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A way' (with 'in') signals SAVEIN rearranged. 'Floating assets' sounds financial but means a country's fleets of warships.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation's warships float, and they are military resources, hence assets.

clue.text: Not much energy for a Cambridge exam

parts.note: little means not much
go means energy or vigour

explanation.surface: A student lacking drive facing a test at Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'little go' was the old name for the first-year examination at Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical name for the preliminary examination taken by Cambridge undergraduates.

clue.text: Noted mistakes in Latin

parts.note: suggests errors made in a Latin text, but means the Latin word for listed errors

explanation.surface: A complaint about errors spotted in someone's Latin homework.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is Latin for 'things erred', used for a printed list of corrections in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing errors noted in a book uses a Latin plural meaning 'mistakes'.

clue.text: Painter individual in metrical composition

indicators.note: the individual goes inside the poem

parts.note: verse is writing in metre
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: An artist singled out within a poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Paolo Veronese was a sixteenth-century Venetian artist.
